title: Best Icon Designers (2026): How to Hire One for Your Project
description: How to hire an icon designer for apps, websites or products: what the package should include, file formats, price factors and red flags.
intro: Icons guide people through apps and websites, and an app icon is often the first thing users see. A good icon set is consistent in style, clear at small sizes and delivered in the formats developers need. Icon projects go wrong when icons are designed one at a time with no shared rules, or delivered only as large images. This guide helps you order icons that work everywhere.

faq.q: Which file format should icons be in?
faq.a: Usually SVG for websites and apps, plus PNG at specific sizes if needed. Ask your developer which formats and sizes they want.
A group of icons designed with the same grid, line weight, corner style and colors, so they look like a family. Consistency matters more than any single icon.

faq.q: How is an app icon different?
faq.a: An app icon represents the whole app in stores and on home screens. It must be recognizable at small sizes and meet each store's size and shape guidelines.

faq.q: Can I use free icon libraries instead?
faq.a: Often, yes, for common actions. Custom icons make sense for brand-specific actions or a distinctive look. Check the license of any library.
Confirm that custom icons are yours to use commercially.
